 Court Delivered The Following:

 Nc: 2024:Khc-D:11484
 Mfa No. 101987 of 2016
 Oral Judgment
This appeal is filed by the claimant/injured seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved
by judgment and award dated 13.1.2016 passed in Mvc No.171/2013 on the file of Member,
Mact-Ii Bagalkot1.
2.

Sri. D.V. Pattar, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding meager compensation of Rs.2,50,348/-, which is contrary to the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Master Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited & Another2.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited & Another2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he seeks to re-assess the same by allowing the appeal.

3. Per contra, learned counsel Smt. Aruna Deshpande for respondent No.2/Insurer supports the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal and submits that the Tribunal taking note of aforesaid judgment in Master Mallikarjun, has awarded just and proper compensation, which does not call for enhancement.
Thus, seeks dismissal of appeal.
'Tribunal', for short 2014(14) SCC 396 NC: 2024:KHC-D:11484 4.
I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.

5. The pleadings and evidence on record indicate that Kumari Chaitra met with road accident on 28.9.2012 and sustained fractures indicated in the Wound Certificate at Ex.P4, which is not disputed by the parties to the proceedings.
In support of the claim, three witnesses were examined namely, father of minor claimant as PW1 and two doctors as PW2 and PW3.
The medical evidence on record indicates that the appellant has sustained 25% disability to the whole body.

Taking note of the same and by applying the principles laid down in Master Mallikarjun's case supra, this Court re- assesses the compensation as under:
Pain and suffering and loss of amenities Rs.3,00,000/- Discomfort, inconvenience &
loss of earnings to the parents during hospitalization Rs. 25,000/- Medical and incidental expense s Rs. 39,098/-
------------------
Total Rs.3,64,098/-
In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
Kumari Chaitra D/O Ashok Hodlur vs Maktumsab @ Munnasab Peersab Attar on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182986901/
2
ORDER a) Appeal stands partly allowed.

NC: 2024:KHC-D:11484 b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified holding that the appellant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,64,098/- as against Rs.2,50,348/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

d) The respondent/Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
e) On such deposit, the same shall be released in favour of the appellant/claimant.

f) Draw modified award accordingly.
g) No order as to costs.
Sd/-
(VIJAYKUMAR A.PATIL) JUDGE JTR/ct-an Kumari Chaitra D/O Ashok Hodlur vs Maktumsab @ Munnasab Peersab Attar on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182986901/
